title: Engagement & Renewal QBR Templates: Growth + Enterprise Playbooks
content:
Purpose: A compact, practical pair of QBR deck templates (Standard / Enterprise) plus a lightweight renewal tracker and playbook snippets. This is intended as a working draft for CS reps to copy/paste into Google Slides and modify per customer. Focus: outcomes, adoption signals, risk mitigation, and clear next steps tied to renewal/expansion outcomes.

Overview of deliverables in this file:
- Standard QBR deck outline (30–45 min) — for SMB / Mid-market customers
- Enterprise QBR deck outline (60–90 min) — for strategic accounts needing deeper ops & roadmap review
- Minimal renewal tracker CSV schema (column list + usage examples)
- Compact playbook snippets: Risk Mitigation, Expansion Motions, Exec Sponsorship Ask
- Prep checklist for CSMs + Customer pre-read template

---

1) Standard QBR (30–45m) — Purpose: show value, diagnose blockers, align on renewal milestone
- Slide 1: Title + Attendees + Goal for this meeting
  Speaker note: keep to one sentence: "Agree on health state and 90d plan tied to renewal." Confirm decision maker present.
- Slide 2: Quick wins since last QBR (3 bullets, % improvement where possible)
  Example bullets: "Average latency to first token improved 18% after 2/1 runtime patch; query error rate down from 1.8% → 0.4%; Key workflow X used by 42% of active seats (up from 29%)."
- Slide 3: Usage snapshot (last 90 days)
  Bullets to display: total API calls, tokens generated, top 3 endpoints, top 3 users/teams, peak QPS and outage incidents.
  Speaker note: highlight 1 metric that ties directly to the customer’s ROI hypothesis.
- Slide 4: Health signals + risk flags (NURTURE mini-score)
  Explain NURTURE: N=NPS feedback snippets, U=Usage breadth, R=Reliability (SLOs), T=Time-to-value (latency/response), U=User churn at feature level, R=Requests for features/bugs, E=Engagement cadence.
  Attach a 1–5 color-coded score.
- Slide 5: Top 3 blockers & proposed fixes (owner + ETA)
  Template rows: blocker | impact | proposed fix | owner | due
- Slide 6: Expansion opportunities (quantified) — recommended motion (pilot, seat expansion, feature bundle)
  Include projected ARR uplift and minimal ask (e.g., "+10 seats for 60-day pilot -> estimated $X MRR uplift").
- Slide 7: Renewal status & asks
  Show current contract end date, renewal cadence, target ARR, and three asks (Exec intro, budget alignment, technical checkpoint).
- Slide 8: Action plan & owners (next 90d milestones)
  3–5 measurable milestones with owners and dates.
- Slide 9: Appendix / data links (logs, perf dashboards, evals)

Timing guidance: 10m wins + usage, 8m health & blockers, 12m expansion & renewal discussion, 5–10m Q&A & next steps.

Notes on tone: concise, outcome-oriented, avoid long technical deep-dives in standard QBR. If technical follow-up needed, schedule a separate ops/infra review.

---

2) Enterprise QBR (60–90m) — Purpose: strategic alignment, roadmap-level partnership, SLA & security review, renewal + multi-year plan
- Slide 1: Executive summary + desired outcome of this meeting (1 page)
  Template: "Confirm renewal posture and agree on a joint 12-month success plan to reach X outcome (e.g., 30% automation of manual review)."
- Slide 2: Strategic business context (customer’s company goals & how Redwood maps to them)
  Bring explicit quotes from customer execs / success metrics.
- Slide 3: Executive health dashboard (C-level view)
  Metrics: business outcome metric (e.g., time-to-decision), cost per inference, adoption across org, SLA compliance, security posture summary.
- Slide 4: Program milestones (past year) — outcomes vs commitments
  One-row per milestone: commitment | outcome | delta | lessons learned | next step.
- Slide 5: Tech health deep-dive (breakout tabs: latency + error trends, model drift signals, KV/prefix cache hit rate, quantization impacts)
  Speaker note: include 2–3 slides in appendix with raw charts; show remediation plan if drift detected.
- Slide 6: Compliance & security posture update (if applicable)
  Items: audit findings, log retention, KMS integration status, private deployment roadmap items.
- Slide 7: Risk register (top 5 risks, likelihood, impact, mitigation owner)
  Include risk heatmap graphic (suggested labels: High/Medium/Low).
- Slide 8: Renewal & commercial proposal options (tiered):
  Option A: Renew current + 10% seats — benefits/cost; Option B: Dedicated pool commitment (improves latency SLA); Option C: Private deployment pilot (for regulated workloads).
  Show short-term ROI for each.
- Slide 9: Joint roadmap (12 months) + decision points
  Highlight which items require budget, which can be experimental.
- Slide 10: Governance cadence & RACI (who signs off on what + meeting cadence)
- Slide 11: Ask list — specific executive asks (intro to CFO, legal timeline, procurement owner)
- Slide 12: Open items & next steps (owners + due dates)
- Appendix: supplementary charts, raw event logs, evals, contact list, escalation path.

Enterprise meeting facilitation notes: Plan pre-reads 3–5 days ahead; schedule separate breakout tracks (Technical, Product, Procurement) during the meeting so each stakeholder gets targeted time.

---

3) Minimal renewal tracker schema (CSV friendly) — recommended columns (keep small for quick triage):
- customer_id, account_name, rep, renewal_date, contract_value_yr, committed_tokens, actual_tokens_90d, health_score (1-10), risk_tags (comma), last_engagement_date, exec_sponsor, next_action, next_action_due, notes

Example row: "RDW-112, Acme Payments, Leah Martinez, 2024-09-15, 180000, 1.2B, 1.1B, 7, usage-drop, 2024-02-28, CFO John Doe, technical deep-dive scheduled, need to demo batching savings"

Quick filters to add in Sheets: "risk_tags contains churn"; conditional format renewal_date < 60 days = red.

---

4) Compact playbook snippets (copyable into Slack or playbook doc)
A) Risk Mitigation (usage drop / exec disengagement) — immediate 7–14 day plan
  Day 0: Notify internal triage (CS + Solutions Engineer + AE) — set owner
  Day 1–3: Run short ops review: token usage by endpoint, error logs, latency. If code/regression found, create urgent bug and schedule hotfix window.
  Day 3–7: Customer touchpoints: product owner check-in (usage vs goals), propose 2–4 tactical changes (prefix caching tweak, batching config, model variant).
  Day 7–14: Re-measure health (tokens 7d rolling, errors). If no improvement, propose executive steering call and highlight renewal risk to AE.

B) Expansion Motion (govt / enterprise play) — 90-day pilot template
  Week 0: Exec alignment call (1 pager: success metrics, decision criteria)
  Week 1–4: Technical onboarding (dedicated model variant, integration checkpoints)
  Week 4–8: Use-case optimization + coaching sessions for power users
  Week 8–12: Business value review + recommendation to scale (formal ask: +X seats / dedicated capacity).

C) Exec Sponsorship Ask (email snippet):
  Subject: Quick alignment: 90d plan to deliver X outcome
  Body: Short 3-line value statement, 1–2 bullet asks (intro to procurement / confirm budget quarter), 1 calendar link for 30-min exec sync.

---

5) Prep checklist for CSM (copy into calendar invite)
- Confirm attendees and decision maker presence (call 48h before)
- Publish pre-read with 3 bullets and required data links (3 days before)
- Run internal health sync (CS + Solutions Eng + AE) 2 business days prior
- Prepare 1–pager commercial options + 1–pager technical options
- Prepare a short demo or playback of "top flow" used by the customer (10 minutes)

Customer pre-read template (one page):
- Summary of goals for meeting (one sentence)
- Current health snapshot (top 3 metrics)
- 3 suggested discussion topics + asks from Redwood
- Links: perf dashboard, renewal draft, product brief

---

6) Quick tips + common pitfalls
- Avoid long vendor-centered slides. Center the deck on the customer’s business objectives.
- Quantify impact whenever possible: tie tokens/latency uptime to revenue or cost saved.
- If there are open technical issues, don’t hide them — present a remediation plan and timeline.
- Use the NURTURE mini-score as a conversation starter; it’s intentionally subjective so the customer can help re-calibrate.

---

7) Appendix: Slide bank titles to clone (short names for quick slide assembly)
- "Top 3 Wins"
- "90d Usage Snapshot"
- "Health + NURTURE Score"
- "Top Blockers"
- "Expansion Cases with ROI"
- "Renewal Options"
- "Risk Register"
- "Technical Deep-dive: Latency & Errors"
- "Compliance Summary"

---

Feedback request: Please review for gaps — specifically, does the Enterprise deck include the right compliance checkpoints for private deployments? Add notes or paste an example renewal clause to the linked Confluence page.

Draft history: created by Leah Martinez 2024-02-15; contributions from Jonah (formatting + tracker), Priya (enterprise facilitation tips), Tomás (technical deep-dive appendix).

End of document."
